reasoning: iter-051: switch gauss_rec prelude dispatch from strided (i=w; i+=W) to block-chunked. The strided pattern caused systematic false sharing because 40-byte GaussianCullRec records are NOT aligned to the 64-byte cache line: a single line covers (record[w], partial record[w+1]) so adjacent workers' writes invalidate each other's L1 line on every other record. Blocked dispatch gives each worker a contiguous private slice, eliminating cross-core line traffic and letting the hw prefetcher engage on the sequential reads of covs_2d/means_2d/opacities. Single-trial result: sum_total 306.6 -> 306.9 ms (within ~1ms noise floor measured at ±3 ms across 4 trials). 4-trial average post-change ~303 ms, slightly better than the iter-049 single-trial 306.6 but not above noise. PSNR identical. Keeping the change because (a) it's architecturally correct (no false sharing), (b) cleaner mental model for subsequent iters that may touch the prelude, (c) no regression risk and a likely small (sub-noise) positive trend in averages.
